word_bank.example: In many Western countries, a firm handshake is the standard greeting in business.
It is common to leave a tip of fifteen to twenty percent at American restaurants.
The invitation says RSVP by Friday so the host knows how many people are coming.
We are having a potluck dinner — please bring a dish to share with everyone.
Americans often start conversations with small talk about the weather or sports.
Please join the queue — everyone waits their turn here.
Good table etiquette includes keeping your phone away during a meal.
He gave her a genuine compliment about her presentation at work.
The job interview required a high level of formality — he wore a suit and tie.
It is a custom in many American homes to remove your shoes at the front door.

stage_2_story.text_en: When Moshe received an invitation to his American colleague's dinner party, he was a little nervous. The invitation said RSVP by Tuesday, so he replied immediately to say he would come. He also asked if it was a potluck, and his colleague told him to bring a dessert. On the evening of the party, Moshe arrived with a homemade cake. His colleague greeted him at the door with a warm handshake. The atmosphere was relaxed, but Moshe paid attention to the etiquette — he waited in the queue at the food table and did not take seconds until everyone had been served. He made small talk with the guests standing nearby, asking about their work and the neighbourhood. One guest gave him a lovely compliment about his cake. Later, when Moshe left the restaurant where they had stopped for coffee, he remembered to leave a tip for the server. Walking home, he reflected that American social customs were different from what he was used to, but the formality of the event had made him feel respected and welcome.
